steps.name: Schwarz
steps.text: Last one here!

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: Everyone else!? Any wounded?

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: No worries here.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: None here, either.

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: Communications equipment?

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: Unharmed.

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: Is this its burrow? ...Strange.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: They seemed like sand beasts, at least?

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: Sand beasts, of this size? Over two meters long?

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: ...I've spent the better part of my life in these wastelands, but never have I seen a sand beast capable of digging holes.

steps.name: Schwarz
steps.text: ...These creatures have Originium crystals on their bodies.

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: Possibly biological mutations caused by Originium pollution, then?

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: There's no nomadic cities, no factories and no mines. How does Originium pollution even happen here?

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: Could it have been a Catastrophe's fault?

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: You'd be underestimating nature. Wildlife knows Catastrophes far better than we do. These creatures would've been the first to avoid Originium pollution.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: Cities can be torn apart by Catastrophes while the wildlife emerges untouched

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: —Nature in this world is ruthless when it wants to eliminate you. If you don't have some way of dealing with Originium, your time as a living species won't be long.

steps.name: Schwarz
steps.text: I think... I have a hypothesis. Like ordinary Originium Slugs, the body's outer shell could have absorbed Originium into its makeup, while its innards remain clean and uncorrupted.

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: On that note, has P.R.T.S ever recorded any similar cases?

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: None. Not even for the Ironforge City leakage incident in Columbia, and that's the first thing you'd think of.

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: Sand beasts are docile creatures by nature. Originium shouldn't change them so drastically, and I can't imagine anything short of Arts would make them outright aggressive.

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: Stay vigilant. Don't let your guard down.

steps.name: Schwarz
steps.text: ...Arts? A Caster? I just hope this doesn't complicate things for us.

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: Don't let it worry you too much. We'll continue on as we were, anyhow.

steps.name: Schwarz
steps.text: Understood.

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: Is this... a Rhodes Island emergency rescue signal?

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: Is it another Rhodes Island field team, maybe?
...oh, thank hea......meone finally answered!
...pl......help us......equesting support...

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: This is a Rhodes Island Field Personnel Team. If you receive this, please reply.
This is......Long Spring......Watchtower 33...
...mob......currently...
...they've come in!

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: Calm down! Operator, tell us what's happened!

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: The signal's very poor. They're coming through intermittent.
...help us......plea......ing you—

a.text: An burst of sharp static, and communications break off.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: Well, that's not good.

steps.name: Schwarz
steps.text: What does Watchtower 33 refer to?

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: From the sound of it, it seemed like a Rhodes Island safehouse's code name.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: A safehouse? The mission brief didn't mention any safehouses around here.

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: Truthfully, in a few areas, Rhodes Island will make a habit of hiding some safehouses, out of the way. For use in very particular field missions.

steps.name: Schwarz
steps.text: But we ourselves don't know where Watchtower 33 is.

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: Long Spring... Long Spring...

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: That name rings a faint bell. If you could let me see the map for a second.

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: Hmm...

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: Here, if I'm not mistaken. Following about twenty kilometers north from Trumhill, you should find another canyon. That canyon had a little village near it, I'm sure of it.

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: That village, years ago, had a well. One of the very few reliable water sources for miles around.

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: So that's why it's Long Spring?

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: So. What do we do next? Change of plans?

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: Or we can try and make for Phecon overnight, get in touch with the branch office and see what assistance we can procure from them.

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: ...I worry the operator in the safehouse may not last long enough for that.

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: All of you, keep going until you reach Phecon, and find some support or other there if you can.

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: I'll head for Long Spring and see what the situation is. Don't you worry, I know this land very, very well. Indeed, I can afford to be more flexible on my lonesome.

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: If things get out of hand there, I'll head back for Phecon promptly and join up with you all.

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: That...

steps.name: Schwarz
steps.text: I object.

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: Oh?

steps.name: Schwarz
steps.text: I'm aware how wary it is of me to say our sand-burrowing mutants and the safehouse's distress call might not just be coincidence, but the Sargon barrens demand we must maintain vigilance.

steps.name: Schwarz
steps.text: We are not clear about the area surrounding Long Spring. Given we are not, you would gamble more alone than you can afford, Rangers, sir.

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: I'd also like to recommend we move for Long Spring as one. If things aren't friendly for us, we can still cover for each other, especially during a retreat.

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: That does make sense.

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: Yes, you're right. The old man will listen. I ought to at my age, anyhow. Can't be as spry and reckless as I was in my younger years.

steps.name: Drudge
steps.text: This thing is ugly as sin.

steps.name: Levi
steps.text: Ugliness is a personal thing subject to the eye of each beholder. You ought to be seeing through to what this creature embodies, signifies. See through to the myriad array of evolutionary possibilities that it testifies to.

steps.name: Levi
steps.text: Order is but our own arbitrarily imposed concept which nature suffers. All the world and its beings were, in their primordiality, chaos seized by impermanence.

steps.name: Levi
steps.text: (Russian) Of course, I don't expect any of your sort to understand that in the first place. It's only natural your soft, ignorant little brains can't grasp the grand strokes of the evolutionary scheme.

steps.name: Drudge
steps.text: A language I know, please!

steps.name: Levi
steps.text: Of course, dear sir, setting apart the matter of whether or not it is ugly to you. I must say you are not seeming wholly satisfied with it.

steps.name: Levi
steps.text: Else you would not be looking for me in the first place.

steps.name: Drudge
steps.text: It still isn't strong enough, schoolboy! Your little beastie couldn't even make the lord's escort blink!

steps.name: Levi
steps.text: Surely you do not suppose it was down to the sheer incompetence of your ignorant little mercenaries?

steps.name: Levi
steps.text: These mutant creatures are weapons, just weapons. If they knew tactics for themselves, you could throw every mercenary of yours into the garbage heap the next day.

steps.name: Mercenary
steps.text: Bite it, old coot! I'm going to twist your goddamn head off.

steps.name: Drudge
steps.text: Hold it!

steps.name: Drudge
steps.text: *Sigh* (facepalm).

steps.name: Drudge
steps.text: Listen, schoolboy.

steps.name: Drudge
steps.text: I'm not backing your research so you can talk my ear off about a bunch of high crap. You're here, for me, to solve practical problems.

steps.name: Drudge
steps.text: I acknowledge it, no mistake. Your research is something else.

steps.name: Drudge
steps.text: But! If you can't help me depose of my father with it, then you and your little shop of horrors can walk yourselves into the goddamn garbage heap.

steps.name: Drudge
steps.text: My patience is limited.

steps.name: Levi
steps.text: As is mine. I have explained this to you over and over already, and I do not wish to do it again, because I do not wish to waste my time.

steps.name: Drudge
steps.text: You think you can fool me!

steps.name: Drudge
steps.text: I've poured money into your little 'experiments' for half a year, the likes of which you'll never see in your entire goddamn life. And I don't think I've seen an equal return on it!

steps.name: Drudge
steps.text: Where's that 'cruel and frightening army' you promised me?

steps.name: Drudge
steps.text: Where's that 'might to make the heart know fear', huh?

steps.name: Drudge
steps.text: You think all it takes to keep me happy is a bunch of ugly, swollen, light-up sand beasts?

steps.name: Levi
steps.text: What does it take for you to understand? The fruits of scientific research need time to grow swollen.

steps.name: Levi
steps.text: If money was all it took to accelerate the march of science, to ripen the fruit, I would have long since flown away to the moon by now.

steps.name: Drudge
steps.text: Enough of that. I'll give you two more days. And I want to like what I see.

steps.name: Levi
steps.text: (Russian) Imbecile.

steps.name: Drudge
steps.text: You speak in a language I don't understand one more time, and I'll throw you and all your little creations into the barrenlands to make merry until the sun goes down.

steps.name: Drudge
steps.text: Go on, try me.

steps.name: Levi
steps.text: *Sigh*.

steps.name: Levi
steps.text: Fetch me some corpses.

steps.name: Drudge
steps.text: Come again?

steps.name: Levi
steps.text: Bring me corpses! People's corpses, corpses like the ones you leave behind! Any will do.

steps.name: Levi
steps.text: Of course, ones blighted by the Originium infection will do even better.

steps.name: Drudge
steps.text: What the hell do you need those for?

steps.name: Mercenary
steps.text: You bastard old coot. Now you want to insult the dead, huh!

steps.name: Levi
steps.text: Did you not want the 'might to make the heart know fear'?

steps.name: Levi
steps.text: Then do not hang yourself up on all that pernicious, useless witter you might otherwise call 'ethics'.

steps.name: Levi
steps.text: The corpses, bring them to me. I would like to have you see something interesting.

steps.name: Mercenary
steps.text: Chief, this goes completely against the Lord Ameer of Bayalir's great commandments. The old coot is trying to dupe you.

steps.name: Drudge
steps.text: You want to take the dead and raise me some Zhayedans?

steps.name: Levi
steps.text: I do not know whatever this ghoulish thing you call a Zhayedan is, but rest assured you will find confidence in the fruits of my scientific research.

steps.name: Mercenary
steps.text: Chief, I don't think...

steps.name: Drudge
steps.text: Shut up!

steps.name: Drudge
steps.text: Old boy, I want you to listen carefully.

steps.name: Drudge
steps.text: You might think you're the peak of intelligence. You might think you've seen every move on the board. You might think there's nothing you don't know.

steps.name: Drudge
steps.text: But don't think about playing a fast one on me. I've gotten to know your kind all too well.

steps.name: Drudge
steps.text: Everyone like you dies because they think they're too goddamn smart to die.

steps.name: Drudge
steps.text: The only reason I still put up with you is because you're still useful.

steps.name: Drudge
steps.text: I can get you what you need.

steps.name: Drudge
steps.text: But don't disappoint me. Because you will not like what comes after.

steps.name: Levi
steps.text: Well, then, what else can I possibly say?

steps.name: Levi
steps.text: Good luck to you.

steps.name: Drudge
steps.text: You're still alive. Don't forget who you have to thank for it.

steps.name: Drudge
steps.text: Without me, your research would amount to a pat of bullshit.

steps.name: Drudge
steps.text: If not for me, you'd be six months dead, rotting in this ore mine.

steps.name: Drudge
steps.text: (Sargonian) Head in your ass.

steps.name: Drudge
steps.text: I'm leaving you two here. Watch him.

steps.name: Mercenary
steps.text: Got it, boss.

steps.name: Levi
steps.text: (Russian) Gaggle of imbeciles. Every second I spend talking to you is spent killing off my precious braincells.

a.text: The aged scholar reaches the depths of the caverns.
Meandering tunnels lined by frames of cast concrete, set in a particular yet strange pattern.
The things in here were never meant to be here.
Within gray-white metal walls, instruments and devices not of this world wind up into operation.
And within a culture chamber, manufactured of clear glass, Originium enveloped in connective tissue floats.
It contracts. It relaxes. It convulses.

steps.name: Levi
steps.text: (Russian) Originium...

steps.name: Levi
steps.text: (Russian) It boggles my mind that this world has such an extraordinary existence gracing it.

steps.name: Levi
steps.text: (Russian) Yet somehow, these locals fear it in their ignorance. Fear what evolution this great power brings with it.

steps.name: Levi
steps.text: (Russian) But no, oh, of course, they should be afraid.

steps.name: Levi
steps.text: (Russian) For the fool fears the unknown. The fool fears might. The fool fears progress...

steps.name: Levi
steps.text: (Russian) Ignorants, oh, you ignorants.
